Class Renderer

java.lang.Object
com.sbancuz.offscreen.window.Renderer
public final class Renderer extends Object
Draws a hosted GUI into a texture, then copies that texture to its desktop window.

There are two OpenGL contexts (independent sets of graphics state). Minecraft's primary context draws the GUI into an offscreen framebuffer, or FBO. The native window's secondary context then reads the shared texture and presents it. Textures can be shared between these contexts; framebuffer objects themselves cannot. That is why framebuffer and presentationFramebuffer are separate.

All methods run on the client thread. The caller must select the correct context: ordinary drawing/allocation/disposal use Minecraft's context; present(int, int) and disposePresentation() use the owning native window's context. Pair successful beginFrame(int, int, int, int) calls with endFrame(Minecraft) in a finally block. This object stores one frame's saved state and is not reentrant.

    • isTimeToRender

      public boolean isTimeToRender()
      Claims the next frame slot using a monotonic nanosecond clock. A capped frame advances the deadline; an unlimited rate permits every call. Actual drawing speed also depends on Minecraft's render loop and hardware.
      Returns:
      true when the caller should draw now, false when rate-limited

    • setFocused

      public void setFocused(boolean focused)
      Selects the focused or background frame budget from configuration. A rate change resets the deadline so the next frame need not wait.
      Parameters:
      focused - whether the owning native window has input focus

    • setBackground

      public void setBackground(@Nullable Runnable background)
      Replaces the optional drawing callback behind the GUI. It runs after clearing but before the standard GUI projection is installed; custom rendering must establish any projection/state it needs.
      Parameters:
      background - callback, or null to draw only the clear color

    • beginFrame

      public void beginFrame(int width, int height, int guiWidth, int guiHeight)
      Borrows primary-context state and prepares the allocated target for GUI drawing. Call ensureCorrectSize(int, int) with the drawable dimensions first, and proceed only if it returns true. Keep Minecraft's context current. A background-callback failure restores the borrowed state before propagating; after a normal return, the caller must invoke endFrame(Minecraft).
      Parameters:
      width - target width in drawable pixels
      height - target height in drawable pixels
      guiWidth - width in Minecraft's scaled GUI units
      guiHeight - height in Minecraft's scaled GUI units

    • endFrame

      public void endFrame(net.minecraft.client.Minecraft mc)
      Returns primary-context graphics state after one successful frame entry. The explicit snapshot also repairs Minecraft's cached state so its next draw does not skip a necessary driver call based on stale cached values.
      Parameters:
      mc - client whose display dimensions describe the outer viewport

    • present

      public void present(int pixelWidth, int pixelHeight)
      Copies the shared image onto the native window's default framebuffer. The owning secondary context must already be current. This does not swap the native window buffers; the caller does that after this method returns. A GL error is logged and produces a conspicuous magenta fallback frame.
      Parameters:
      pixelWidth - current destination drawable width; clamped to at least one
      pixelHeight - current destination drawable height; clamped to at least one

    • fbo

      public int fbo()
      Returns a borrowed primary-context FBO name; callers must not delete it.
      Returns:
      drawing framebuffer ID, or zero before allocation/after disposal

    • ensureCorrectSize

      public boolean ensureCorrectSize(int width, int height)
      Reuses or reallocates the primary-context color/depth/stencil render target. Old storage is discarded on resize. The current draw/read framebuffer, renderbuffer, and 2D texture bindings are restored after allocation attempts.
      Parameters:
      width - requested positive drawable width in pixels
      height - requested positive drawable height in pixels
      Returns:
      true for a complete matching target; false for invalid dimensions or an incomplete framebuffer

    • dispose

      public void dispose()
      Deletes primary-context drawing resources. Repeated calls are harmless. Secondary-context presentation resources require disposePresentation().

    • disposePresentation

      public void disposePresentation()
      Deletes the presentation FBO while its owning secondary context is current. Call before destroying that native context; repeated calls are harmless.
